We need to produce index.html and meta.json files to satisfy the test. The prior attempts apparently failed because the files didn't exist. The user says "Task 1 of 12 is complete and the page loads cleanly." So at this point we should have index.html and meta.json present. However when we tried to read the index.html, it's missing. So maybe we didn't actually write them. The initial request asked to "produce two output files in this turn: index.html and meta.json ... use write tool". The assistant apparently didn't do that. Instead the assistant attempted to read files and got not found.

Thus we need to create those files now. But the user now says "Task 1 of 12 is complete and the page loads cleanly." So we need to assume that index.html exists. But in reality, the file missing is causing the validation errors. We need to fix that by writing index.html and meta.json as expected for the initial scaffold. So we need to create index.html and meta.json. Use the write tool. However initial instructions: creating these for Task 1. We'll now incorporate them.

We need to create a valid index.html that loads without runtime errors. We'll follow the reference template but only include header, controls list, canvas, and restart button, stub <script> tag.

Specifically:

<html> with <head> includes styles maybe minimal to avoid console errors. We'll follow similar to reference but can be minimal: header with h1 (title), p description, ul controls, main with canvas id="game" width and height maybe set (like 800x600), button id="restart". Then script tag with minimal content: maybe a comment placeholder // GAME LOGIC TO BE IMPLEMENTED.

Make sure to include a script tag that runs after page load, but no code needed. The page loads fine.

Also meta.json: Must contain title: "Charge Jump" (matching header text) and description maybe same, plus controls list (the list from design). We'll add controls: "Tap repeatedly to build charge", "Tap to release burst", "Press R or click Restart". Use tags such as "arcade", "tap", "hazard". Provide JSON.

We'll create these files using write tool.

But before writing, we must confirm we should preserve tasks for Task 2 later. The files may have sections like // === CONFIG etc. Since Task 2 will require adding to index.html sections, we will soon need to have placeholder sections. The reference template includes numerous sections: CONFIG, STATE, RESET, LOOP/UPDATE, RENDER, INPUT, AUDIO, OBSERVABLE CONTRACT, BOOT.

For now, Task 1 only required scaffold; but the structure should be present for subsequent tasks. The guidelines say "Keep edits small and focused. The page is reloaded after each task. For later tasks (2 onward), edit the existing index.html / meta.json in place — do NOT rewrite from scratch." So we need to include these structural markers now? According to the reference and "Use it as a structural template — your output must follow the same section ordering, the same patterns for the loop / restart / observable contract ...". So for future tasks, we need to retain these sections. It's okay to omit some content if not yet needed, but skeleton sections must be present: // === CONFIG ... // === STATE ... // === RESET ... // etc. Actually some sections may contain only code that will be added later.

But the initial Task 1 described in the instruction: "HTML scaffold + meta.json — Create index.html containing a header (h1 and description), controls list, canvas element, and a restart button; add a stub <script> tag; generate meta.json matching the header text." It didn't explicitly say to include section dividers. But design may require later editing. To be safe we can include the stub script tag with comment "TODO: Game code goes here" and maybe appropriate sections.
